title: Product Comparison Video: Side by Side | AIVideosUGC
description: Make a product comparison video that puts two of your own colors, sizes, or models side by side. Get a 1:1 or 16:9 clip for your listing or Shorts. Try it.
h1: Make a Product Comparison Video of Your Own Options
lead: A product comparison video helps shoppers choose between your own colors, sizes, or models. Upload a photo of both, say what sets them apart, and get a short side-by-side clip.
intro: Two of your products stand next to each other so buyers can compare them at a glance. Our sample pairs a charcoal travel tumbler with a cream one on a light counter: same shape, different finish.

Comparison clips settle the small questions that hold up a sale, like which color, which size, or which lid. Use it for your own range only, such as two bottle capacities, a standard and a deluxe kit, or old packaging next to new. Pick 1:1 or 16:9 for a product listing, or 9:16 for YouTube Shorts. When size is what sets the two apart, add a still size comparison photo next to an object shoppers know.
tip: Shoot both products together in one photo, then spell out the difference in plain words, like "black tumbler on the left, cream on the right, same size."

steps.t: Upload both options in one photo
steps.d: Set the two products side by side on a plain surface so the video keeps them at the right scale.
Describe what sets them apart: color, size, lid, or finish. Use 6 seconds for a fast glance or 15 for a slow pan across both.
Add names, sizes, and prices above each product in Canva or CapCut after you download.

ideas.d: Stand your small and large bottles together so buyers see the real difference in height.
Show your updated design next to the previous one so returning customers recognize it.
Compare one item with your gift set to show which pieces come in the bundle.

faq.q: Can I compare my product with another brand's?
faq.a: No. Use this template to compare options from your own range, like two colors or two sizes. Requests that include other companies' logos or trademarks may be refused.

faq.q: Can the video show capacity, weight, or price?
faq.a: Add specs like these as text in your editor after downloading. Generated numbers aren't always accurate, so it's safer to type them yourself.

faq.q: Which aspect ratio should I choose?
faq.a: Square 1:1 works well in product galleries and feeds. Widescreen 16:9 suits a video in your product description. Vertical 9:16 is for YouTube Shorts and other phone-first feeds.

overview.h2: Compare what the camera can actually show
overview.d: A side-by-side clip is useful for color, size, finish, included pieces, or packaging. Keep the two items in one stable composition and let viewers inspect the difference; put performance claims and exact specifications in your product listing.

overview.h2: Keep the comparison about your range
overview.d: Use this template for your own variants, sizes, or bundles. It can clarify a choice without naming or implying a competing brand, and it leaves the final decision with the shopper.

input_guide.h2: Photograph both options for fair scale

items.d: Place both items on the same plain surface so the scene does not invent a scale difference.
Front views work for color and packaging; a three-quarter view can reveal a lid, handle, or side port on both products.
A small space between the options gives each label and silhouette room after the clip is downloaded.
Say charcoal versus cream, 12-ounce versus 20-ounce, or single item versus set instead of asking for a general comparison.
The clip can make color, form, packaging, or included pieces easy to inspect in one frame.
Use 1:1 for a listing or feed, 16:9 for a wide product section, 9:16 for Shorts, or 4:3 and 3:4 for other crops.
Six, ten, fifteen, and thirty seconds cost 24, 40, 60, and 120 credits; you see that amount before creating a version.
A small and large bottle stand on a counter at the same distance, with the height difference visible from base to cap.
Matte black and brushed steel headphones rotate on matching stands while the ear-cup finish catches light.
Two boxes sit side by side on a shelf, then the camera passes across the changed front panel.
One mug stays left while the gift set opens on the right to reveal its extra pieces.

after_download.h2: Add facts the scene cannot show

items.d: Place the variant name, size, color, or model above the correct side.
Use current listing data for price, capacity, dimensions, and included pieces.
Describe the visible difference without adding a performance winner the clip cannot prove.
